42919988|en|claude-sonnet-5-5.summary: The Review addresses the shift in cardiac pacing from conventional right ventricular apical pacing towards physiological activation of the native conduction system. It states that decades of evidence have established that chronic right ventricular pacing induces ventricular dyssynchrony, contributing to pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and adverse clinical outcomes. Conduction system pacing engages the intrinsic His-Purkinje network and is described as preserving or restoring the natural ventricular activation sequence. His bundle pacing, the earliest form, provided proof of concept but is limited by technical challenges and high capture thresholds. Left bundle branch area pacing has become the dominant modality, offering greater procedural success, lead stability and broader applicability. Its applications span management of bradycardia, prevention of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and cardiac resynchronization therapy in heart failure. Bachmann bundle area pacing is presented as an emerging atrial counterpart that captures a preferential interatrial conduction pathway. This approach reduces interatrial conduction delay and produces a more physiological atrial activation sequence than conventional right atrial appendage pacing. The authors state that it might therefore help to prevent atrial fibrillation. The Review unites ventricular and atrial strategies under the principle of physiological pacing, describes their mechanistic basis and technical evolution, appraises the latest evidence from randomized trials, and addresses practical questions in clinical application. It indicates where more evidence is required.

42933911|en|claude-sonnet-5-5.summary: Calcium fracture is a metric used to assess lesion preparation success. The investigators had previously shown that OCT misses approximately half of these fractures, and the sensitivity of IVUS, the most commonly used intravascular imaging modality, for detecting fractures after IVL was unknown. This ex vivo study aimed to assess the frequency and characteristics of calcium fracture on IVUS compared with OCT and gold standard micro-CT. Heavily calcified coronary artery cadaveric vessels were used: 5 cadaveric hearts with 15 coronary lesions. OCT, IVUS and micro-CT were obtained before and after IVL treatment. Fracture detection rates and appearance patterns were compared across modalities, and receiver operating characteristic analyses evaluated OCT-measured fracture width thresholds for IVUS detectability. Compared with micro-CT, OCT and IVUS significantly underestimated fracture occurrence, and OCT had higher detection sensitivity than IVUS (P < 0.05 by McNemar's test). Narrow linear nondisplaced fractures identified on OCT were frequently undetectable on IVUS or appeared as subtle hyperechoic shadows. Fracture width was strongly associated with IVUS detectability; OCT fracture width >115 μm was identified by IVUS with an AUC of 0.99 (95% CI 0.98-1.00), sensitivity 100% and specificity 92%. The authors conclude that OCT and IVUS underestimate IVL-induced calcium fractures compared with micro-CT, that IVUS has lower sensitivity than OCT, and that IVUS detectability depends strongly on fracture width.

42933915|en|claude-sonnet-5-5.summary: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is common in patients undergoing mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER), and the prognostic significance of periprocedural PH changes was described as uncertain. The study aimed to evaluate the association between periprocedural PH patterns and clinical outcomes after M-TEER and to identify predictors of residual and new-onset PH. The OCEAN-Mitral registry prospectively enrolled 3,764 patients with severe mitral regurgitation treated with M-TEER. Among 3,484 patients with paired echocardiographic tricuspid regurgitation pressure gradient (TRPG) data, PH was defined as TRPG >31 mm Hg. Patients were classified as no PH (1,432; 41.1%), normalized PH (763; 21.9%), new-onset PH (298; 8.6%) or residual PH (991; 28.4%) according to pre- and postprocedural PH status. The primary endpoint was 2-year cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization, which occurred in 17.6%, 18.1%, 27.2% and 27.6% of the four groups, respectively (P < 0.001). Normalized PH showed outcomes comparable to no PH (adjusted HR 0.98; 95% CI 0.78-1.24). New-onset PH (HR 1.46; 95% CI 1.10-1.93) and residual PH (HR 1.37; 95% CI 1.13-1.68) were independently associated with adverse outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression identified severe tricuspid regurgitation, baseline TRPG >50 mm Hg and tricuspid annular dilation as predictors of residual PH. 42949674|en|claude-sonnet-5-5.why_it_matters: This narrative review addresses how high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) results are classified in clinical practice, organized around 4 interpretive domains. According to the abstract, hs-cTn assays detect myocardial injury but have created a problem of classification, with nonischemic injury mislabeled as secondary MI and chronic myocardial injury dismissed once infarction is excluded.
42949674|en|claude-sonnet-5-5.key_finding: The review organizes hs-cTn interpretation into 4 domains: assay properties of hs-cTnI and hs-cTnT (assay-specific and sex-specific thresholds, clearance kinetics, interference); serial testing, including the ESC 0/1h and 0/2h algorithms, point-of-care platforms and AI-based decision support; the Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction; and non-ACS conditions. It states that nonischemic myocardial injury is frequently mislabeled as secondary MI, contributing to overdiagnosis of MI. Chronic myocardial injury is described as carrying a risk of subsequent MI or cardiovascular death approaching that of primary MI.
42949674|en|claude-sonnet-5-5.summary: The review starts from the premise that hs-cTn assays have solved the detection of myocardial injury but created a problem of classifying it. Abnormal troponin concentrations are described as common across a wide spectrum of cardiac and systemic disease. The authors state that misclassification occurs in both directions: nonischemic myocardial injury is frequently mislabeled as secondary MI, contributing to overdiagnosis of MI, while chronic myocardial injury, with a risk of subsequent MI or cardiovascular death approaching that of primary MI, is routinely dismissed once infarction has been excluded. The article is a narrative review. It argues that accurate classification cannot be delegated to an algorithm and rests on 4 domains. The first domain covers the analytical and biological properties of hs-cTnI and hs-cTnT, including assay-specific and sex-specific thresholds, clearance kinetics, and sources of analytical interference and false-positive results. The second covers the capabilities and limitations of guideline-endorsed serial testing, including the ESC 0/1h and 0/2h algorithms, point-of-care platforms, and artificial intelligence-based decision support. The third covers application of the Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction, in particular the distinctions between myocardial injury, necrosis and infarction, and between diagnosis and risk stratification. The fourth covers non-acute coronary syndrome conditions in which troponin elevation is expected: chronic kidney disease, heart failure, sepsis, tachyarrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, takotsubo syndrome and others. The authors provide bedside guidance for suspected secondary MI, the observe zone, and troponin elevation without a dynamic pattern. The review also covers emerging troponin biology: clearance, proteolysis and fragmentation, macrotroponin, antitroponin autoantibodies, and extracellular vesicle-associated troponin. According to the authors, these developments may eventually allow the assay itself to carry more of the interpretive burden, which until then rests with the clinician.

42912400|en|claude-sonnet-5-5.summary: The study addressed the long-term risk of all-cause, CVD and CHD mortality associated with premature advanced subclinical atherosclerosis, since the long-term prognostic value of CAC in young adults is described as unclear. It was a cohort study using the CAC Consortium dataset, a retrospectively assembled cohort of referred individuals with clinically indicated CAC scans from four US institutions. Adults aged 30 to 45 years were included and followed for a median of 22.6 years, with underlying cause of mortality as the outcome. The exposure was CAC score greater than 90%, compared with a CAC score of 0. Multivariable regression models for time-to-event analysis were adjusted for age, sex and traditional atherosclerotic CVD risk factors. Cumulative incidence was derived in 5-year increments up to 30 years using Kaplan-Meier and Weibull modeling. The analysis included 12 847 participants (mean age 40.5 years; 9922 [77.2%] male): 9262 (72.1%) had CAC score of 0, 1626 (12.7%) had a score between 75% and 90%, and 1703 (13.3%) had a score greater than 90%. There were 624 deaths (149 CVD and 81 CHD). Adjusted hazard ratios for CAC score greater than 90% vs 0 were 1.87 (95% CI, 1.54-2.27) for all-cause, 2.60 (95% CI, 1.77-3.82) for CVD and 3.71 (95% CI, 2.24-6.16) for CHD mortality. Modeled 30-year risk was higher in the CAC greater than 90% group than in the CAC 0 group for all-cause (12.9% vs 7.5%), CVD (4.5% vs 1.5%) and CHD (3.0% vs 0.6%) mortality. The authors conclude that young adults with a CAC score greater than 90% face significantly higher long-term risk of all-cause, CVD and CHD mortality, with potential implications for guiding intensification of preventive intervention.

The abstract describes these questions as contested, with US labeling having moved in 2 opposing directions within 16 months.
42924843|en|claude-sonnet-5-5.key_finding: Low endogenous testosterone was consistently associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, which the review considers most plausibly a marker of multimorbidity rather than causation. TRAVERSE established that physiologic transdermal testosterone replacement therapy was noninferior to placebo for 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events over ∼3 years, within a permissive margin and against a 61% discontinuation rate. 42924843|en|claude-sonnet-5-5.summary: The review addresses whether low endogenous testosterone is causal for cardiovascular disease and how the cardiovascular risk of testosterone replacement therapy should now be classified. The authors describe both questions as contested, with US labeling having moved in 2 opposing directions within 16 months. It is a targeted narrative review reported in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles. MEDLINE and primary regulatory documents were searched from January 2000 through July 2026. Evidence was graded with a prespecified 3-tier structured author-consensus rating separating established randomized findings, unresolved secondary signals, and evidentiary absence. Low endogenous testosterone is consistently associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, but most plausibly marks multimorbidity rather than causation. TRAVERSE established that physiologic transdermal testosterone replacement therapy was noninferior to placebo for 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events over ∼3 years, within a permissive margin and against a 61% discontinuation rate. Observational analyses linking normalization to lower mortality were not reproduced under randomization. Atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, fracture and noncalcified plaque progression remain unresolved. Blood pressure rises across the class; on ambulatory monitoring the magnitude differs by individual product rather than by route. Long-term exposure and nontransdermal formulations remain untested, and the age-related-hypogonadism limitation of use is now proposed for removal. The authors state that noninferiority over 3 years is not to be read as long-term clinical equivalence.

Denominators of 52 and 51 (103) do not match the 104 patients analysed, and the reason is not explained. The abstract states TPV regression P = .05. The abstract's own description of the TPV and NCPV comparison refers to '-38%' LDL-C reduction etc. exactly as quoted. Abstract does not specify whether the 104 analysed patients are the full randomized population. Conclusion phrase 'supporting the potential for partial reversal' is the authors' wording and is attributed to them.
